title: How to Fix Your Focus in One Day
author: Sharran Srivatsaa
summary: Entrepreneur Sharran Srivatsaa, who has built two billion-dollar businesses and is now building a third with Alex and Leila Hormozi, lays out three personal focus frameworks he credits with protecting his attention amid constant distraction. The first, "Creating Tomorrow, Today," is a nightly journaling habit inherited from his father: planning the next day's full task list before the current day ends, so distractions and other people's priorities do not fill the calendar by default. The second, "Zones & Bones," treats time as an investment portfolio split into strictly separated Work, Family, and Personal zones, each allotted a deliberate number of weekly hours ("bones") with a hard rule against mixing zones. The third is a three-stage "pull system" — capture every task into a single inbox, triage it into Today/This Week/Scheduled/Someday categories two to three times daily, and execute only from the calendar rather than a running to-do list — designed to eliminate the split attention that comes from tracking tasks in two places (a to-do list and an email inbox) at once. Srivatsaa frames all three as complementary tools that can be adopted incrementally, with the underlying thesis that singularity of focus, achieved by doing fewer things well, is one of the strongest predictors of long-term success.
points: Argues that protecting tomorrow's focus starts the night before: nightly planning of the next day's full task list prevents distractions and other people's priorities from filling an unplanned calendar by default.
Frames time explicitly as investment capital in the "Zones & Bones" model, with a hard rule against mixing Work, Family, and Personal zones — a discipline distinct from merely scheduling more hours.
Identifies a common but underexamined focus-killer: running two parallel to-do systems (an email inbox and a separate task list) that silently split attention and energy.
Prescribes a specific triage cadence — sorting captured tasks into Today, This Week, Scheduled/Waiting, or Someday two to three times daily — to keep a single inbox from becoming a backlog.
Positions singularity of focus, not raw effort or hours logged, as the strongest lever for achieving significant outcomes, tying the frameworks back to a "fewer things, done better" philosophy.
quotes: Every night after dinner, he'd open a leather journal and do two things: Write tomorrow's date. And list everything he'd do the next day. He called it: "Creating tomorrow, today." He never missed a night.
Zones: this is where you invest your time. Bones: this is how many hours each zone gets. This is exactly how I split my time into 3 different zones: Work, Family, and Personal.
My email inbox had become a to-do list itself. This meant all my tasks for the day lived in two separate places instead of one. And it was splitting my focus and energy in half.
I sort them into 4 categories: Today. This Week. Scheduled / Waiting. Someday. I triage my inbox 2-3 times a day. So by the end of the day it should nearly be empty.
Execute means you take the tasks marked Today and invest your time into them on your zones and bones calendar. And so now you're back to working from your calendar, not a to-do list.
Singularity of focus is one of the greatest predictors of your success. Because to do great things, we must do fewer things.
